title: EVENT HORIZON: black hole information (Page curve, evaporation, Hayden-Preskill)
description_md:
## Question

Can the Page curve of an evaporating black hole be reconstructed from quantum information theory, and under which conditions can information be recovered from the radiation? This problem attacks it with exact, verified numerics on finite-dimensional qubit models (no gravity): Page's theorem, sequential evaporation, a Bell-pair Hawking model, scramblers and Hayden-Preskill recovery, computed on an A100 and re-derived by an independent implementation.

**Score:** 8 of 9 key claims independently verified; the verifier corrected the remaining one. Nothing here claims to solve the information paradox.

## Abstract (from the paper)

We report a reproducible set of exact state-vector computations on qubit toy models that are commonly used to discuss the black hole information paradox. (i) The Page curve of Haar-random pure states is reproduced for N = 8..24 qubits and Page's formula is checked at 124 dimension pairs (m, n) up to m·n = 2^24 (max |z| = 2.69, rms z = 1.00). (ii) A sequential "evaporation" protocol with a fresh Haar unitary on the remaining hole at every step is run literally up to N = 14 qubits and with an exact-in-distribution isometry sampler up to N = 26 (one trajectory at N = 27); we give the elementary proof that its whole entropy trajectory has exactly the law of the nested cuts of one Haar state, and the numerics agree. (iii) The Bell-pair model of Hawking emission gives S(R) = k ln 2 to round-off and exceeds the assumed capacity of the remaining hole for every k > N/2. (iv) With local brickwork scramblers the radiation entropy approaches the Page curve only when enough layers are applied per emission; the one-shot half-cut scrambling depth of Haar brickwork grows linearly, D* ≈ 1.87 N + 1.9 layers for N = 8..24 at a 0.05-nat threshold. Scrambled stabilizer (Clifford) states have flat spectra and a mean half-cut entropy *below* the Page value (−0.088 ± 0.015 nats at N = 10), so they never come within 0.05 nats of it. (v) In the Hayden-Preskill setting with a Haar scrambler the measured decoupling distance obeys the bound E T ≤ ½·2^(k−m) (ratio to the finite-d bound 0.83–0.87), with recovery thresholds essentially independent of the hole size for an old hole and shifted by ≈ n_B/2 for a young one. An independent verifier that shares no code with the builders reproduced eight of nine checked claims and corrected the sign of one interpretive statement. All findings are reproductions (class 1), verifications of known relations (class 2) or computational observations inside known models (class 3).

**This work does not solve, and does not claim to solve, the information paradox.** Every model is a finite-dimensional qubit system without gravity. The island formula of semiclassical gravity is summarised in a separate section (Sec. 8) and is neither derived nor tested by anything computed here.

artifact.title: Event Horizon: finite-dimensional numerics around the black hole information paradox
artifact.question: Which standard quantum-information statements about black hole evaporation (Page curve, Page's theorem, sequential evaporation, Bell-pair model, scrambling, Hayden-Preskill) can be reproduced exactly, at what size on one A100, and do they survive independent verification?
artifact.summary: Page's formula is reproduced up to 24 qubits and m*n = 2^24 (max |z| 2.69 over 124 pairs). Sequential Haar evaporation is provably and numerically the same ensemble as one Haar state seen through nested cuts (literal runs to N = 14, isometry sampler to N = 26). The Bell-pair model gives S(R) = k ln 2 to 4.4e-15 and exceeds the assumed hole capacity for k > N/2. Local Haar brickwork needs about 8 layers per emission to stay within about 0.05 nats of Page; scrambled stabilizer states sit 0.088 +- 0.015 nats below Page at N = 10. The Hayden-Preskill decoupling bound holds (measured/bound 0.83-0.87) with thresholds essentially independent of hole size for an old hole. All findings are class 1-3. Finite-dimensional qubit toy models without gravity. Nothing here solves or claims to solve the information paradox; the island formula is not derived or tested. Upgrade (2026-11-15): Renyi Page curves and exact Wishart moments, Marchenko-Pastur entanglement spectra, exact stabilizer-state enumeration (3-design, not 4-design), Petz-decoder Hayden-Preskill thresholds (old hole m* = 1.72-1.75 for n_B = 3..7; young-hole shift 0.2-0.3 qubit below n_B/2), OTOCs, [[5,1,3]] and random-code erasure correction, and an evaluated AMM island formula kept separate from the circuit models. All new results are class 1-3; 5 of 5 new claims re-derived by verify/independent_upgrade.py; one novelty claim (Petz closed form for erasure) retracted after review.
artifact.disclaimer: Finite-dimensional qubit toy models without gravity. Nothing here solves or claims to solve the information paradox; the island formula is not derived or tested.

cycles.question: Does the entanglement entropy of k qubits of a Haar-random N-qubit pure state follow Page's curve, and how close is the mean to Page's exact formula?
cycles.conclusion: Page curve reproduced for N = 8..24 within Monte Carlo error.

cycles.question: How accurately does Monte Carlo over Haar states reproduce Page's formula across many (m, n), and how good are the asymptotic forms?
cycles.conclusion: Page's formula verified at 124 dimension pairs up to m*n = 2^24; the first correction to Page's asymptotic form is +1/(2mn).

cycles.question: Does sequential evaporation (a fresh Haar unitary on the remaining hole before every emitted qubit) differ from a single Haar-random state, in the mean or in the distribution of the entropy trajectory?
cycles.conclusion: Sequential Haar evaporation reproduces Page's mean at every step and no statistically significant difference from the nested-cut law was found; the proof is the invariance argument, not the non-rejection.
cycles.classification: 2 (mean) / 3 (trajectory-level and distribution tests inside a known model)

cycles.question: What does the independent Bell-pair model of Hawking emission give for S(R), and exactly where and why does it part from the unitary model?
cycles.conclusion: The pair model and the unitary model differ for k > N/2 because of independent pair creation, no correlations among quanta, partners that never leave, and a shrinking capacity.

cycles.question: How much local scrambling per emitted qubit is needed for the radiation entropy to follow the Page curve, and do Clifford circuits get there?
cycles.conclusion: About 8 brickwork layers of local Haar gates per emission keep the radiation within roughly 0.05 nats of Page for N = 8..26, and 16 layers within 0.01 nats; one-shot Haar brickwork needs about 1.87 N layers for N = 8..24.

cycles.question: After how many emitted qubits m can a k-qubit diary be recovered from an old (maximally entangled) or young black hole, and does the decoupling bound hold quantitatively?
cycles.conclusion: The decoupling bound holds and is about 15% above the measured mean T; an old hole returns a k-qubit diary after m about k + 1 to k + 3 qubits regardless of size, a young hole needs about n_B/2 more.
cycles.classification: 2 (Haar scrambler: verification of a known relation) / 3 (local scramblers)

cycles.question: Do Renyi-n Page curves and exact Haar trace moments of random pure states match the complex-Wishart closed forms?
cycles.hypothesis: E Tr rho^k from the Wishart permutation sum (Lubkin for k=2) matches Haar Monte Carlo; S_1 matches Page.
assumptions: Haar-random pure states on N qubits (random-matrix model, no dynamics, no gravity)
S_2 compared with -log E[Tr rho^2], which is not E[S_2] (Jensen gap)
cycles.prediction: |z| < 3 against exact S_1 and exact E Tr rho^k for every cut; S_n non-increasing in n.
cycles.falsification_criterion: Any |z| > 4 against an exact moment, or S_n increasing in n.
cycles.method: experiments/f_spectra.py part A/B: N=12, 400 seeds (SeedSequence 202611151/2); 10 (dA,dB) pairs, 10k-40k samples.
cycles.result: N=12 half cut: S_1 = 3.65868 +- 0.00038 vs Page 3.65903; S_2 = 3.4651 +- 0.0005 vs -log Lubkin 3.46598; max |z| 2.48 over 30 moment comparisons.
cycles.verification: verify/independent_upgrade.py V1 (seed 20261116, numpy, no eh/ import): agree=True; Lubkin purity and Tr rho^3 re-derived by MC at (4,4),(8,8),(8,32); builder's N=12 exact purity table reproduced to 0.
critic_objections: S_2 vs -log E[purity] is an approximation (Jensen), not an exact prediction; the 1.8 sigma offset is within it.
The three moments per pair share samples, so z values are correlated.
Renyi Page curves and Wishart moments are textbook (Lubkin 1978; Nadal-Majumdar-Vergassola 2011): reproduction only.
cycles.conclusion: N=12 half cut: S_1 = 3.65868 +- 0.00038 vs Page 3.65903; S_2 = 3.4651 +- 0.0005 vs -log Lubkin 3.46598; max |z| 2.48 over 30 moment comparisons.

cycles.question: Do entanglement spectra follow Marchenko-Pastur, and which diagnostics distinguish Haar, stabilizer and shallow-brickwork ensembles?
cycles.hypothesis: Haar Schmidt spectra converge to MP with O(1/d) moment corrections; stabilizer spectra are exactly flat; GUE-like gap ratios for Haar.
assumptions: Random-matrix model; MP is an asymptotic law
Stabilizer ensemble approximated by depth-6N random Clifford brickwork (convergence checked at N,2N,4N,6N)
cycles.prediction: KS distance to MP shrinks with d; <r> ~ 0.5996 (GUE) for Haar; stabilizer spectra flat to machine precision; stabilizer states a 3-design, not a 4-design.
cycles.falsification_criterion: KS distance not decreasing; non-flat stabilizer spectrum; 4-design property holds.
cycles.method: experiments/f_spectra.py parts B-E (seeds 202611152-202611155); exact enumeration of all stabilizer states n<=4 (6, 60, 1080, 36720).
cycles.result: MP moments match Narayana numbers; KS shrinks with size; stabilizer flatness exact; enumeration exactly a 3-design and not a 4-design.
cycles.verification: verify/independent_upgrade.py V4 (seed 20261116, numpy, no eh/ import): agree=True; stabilizer counts 6/60/1080 re-derived by Clifford-orbit BFS on state vectors.
critic_objections: MP, Atas gap-ratio values and the 3-design/not-4-design property of stabilizer states are literature results (Marchenko-Pastur 1967; Atas et al. 2013; Webb 2016; Zhu 2017; Kueng-Gross 2015): class 1.
Gap ratios of an entanglement spectrum are not a Hamiltonian level-statistics diagnostic; usage is descriptive only.
The 6N brickwork is not exactly uniform over stabilizer states; only convergence of low moments was checked.
cycles.conclusion: MP moments match Narayana numbers; KS shrinks with size; stabilizer flatness exact; enumeration exactly a 3-design and not a 4-design.

cycles.question: How many emitted qubits m does a Petz decoder need to recover a k-qubit diary from an old vs young Haar-scrambled hole?
cycles.hypothesis: Old hole: m* - k = O(1) independent of n_B; young hole: shift about n_B/2 (Hayden-Preskill).
assumptions: All-to-all Haar scrambler at infinite temperature
Petz (transpose) decoder with sigma = 1/d_M: F_Petz <= F_opt <= sqrt(F_Petz) (Barnum-Knill), so m* is decoder-specific
cycles.prediction: m*(F_Petz=0.9) constant in n_B for an old hole; young-old shift approaching n_B/2.
cycles.falsification_criterion: Old-hole m* drifting by more than 0.5 qubit across n_B, or young-hole shift not growing with n_B.
cycles.method: experiments/g_recovery.py g1: k=1, n_B=3..7, 24 seeds (12 at n_B=7), seed 20261115+1000.
cycles.verification: verify/independent_upgrade.py V5 (seed 20261116, numpy, no eh/ import): agree=True; F(m-k=0, n_B=3) = 0.769 +- 0.003 (48 seeds) vs builder 0.765.
critic_objections: The Petz threshold measures one decoder's performance, not information content: I(R D : Q) can be near-maximal while F_Petz < 0.9. Statement downgraded to 'Petz-decoder threshold'.
'Finite-size correction' for the 0.2-0.3 qubit deficit is an untested interpretation; it could equally be decoder suboptimality (sqrt(F_Petz) bracket is wide at F~0.8).
V5 re-uses the builder's Petz formula (independent state construction and sampler only); the formula itself is checked against Kraus composition in tests/test_recovery.py.

cycles.question: How do depolarizing noise on the radiation and finite circuit depth degrade recovery, and how does the infinite-temperature OTOC track it?
cycles.hypothesis: Recovery fidelity decreases smoothly with noise; OTOCs decay to the 2-design value -1/(d^2-1) at the same depth that recovery saturates.
assumptions: beta = 0 OTOC F(t) = 2^-N Tr[W(t) V W(t)^dag V^dag], Pauli W, V
Haar and Clifford brickwork; small N (<= 8 for dense OTOC)
cycles.prediction: Haar average OTOC = -1/(d^2-1); OTOC decay and Petz-fidelity saturation occur at comparable depth.
cycles.falsification_criterion: Haar OTOC mean deviating from -1/(d^2-1) by > 4 sigma; recovery saturating long before or after OTOC decay.
cycles.result: See results/g_recovery.json (g2_noise_D, g2_noise_DR, g3); OTOC and recovery saturate at comparable depths; Clifford purity matches Haar (2-design).
cycles.verification: verify/independent_upgrade.py V3 (seed 20261116, numpy, no eh/ import): agree=True; Haar OTOC N=3: -0.0208 +- 0.0028 vs -1/63 = -0.0159 (z = -1.74).
critic_objections: OTOC decay is necessary but not sufficient for Hayden-Preskill recovery (Yoshida-Kitaev link holds for the Pauli-averaged OTOC only); the 'tracks' statement is a qualitative co-occurrence at one N.
Clifford circuits agreeing with Haar on second moments is guaranteed (2-design), not a finding.
cycles.conclusion: See results/g_recovery.json (g2_noise_D, g2_noise_DR, g3); OTOC and recovery saturate at comparable depths; Clifford purity matches Haar (2-design).

cycles.question: Which erasures of an encoded logical qubit are correctable for [[5,1,3]], random stabilizer and Haar-isometry codes?
cycles.hypothesis: [[5,1,3]] is a perfect tensor (I(R:A) in {0,2} bits); random stabilizer codes give integer I(R:A); Haar codes are never exactly correctable but approximate a Page-type I(R:A).
assumptions: Finite-dimensional QEC models; this does not derive holography
Random stabilizer codes from 10n random 2-qubit Cliffords on random pairs (not exactly uniform)
cycles.prediction: I(R:A) = 2 bits iff |A| >= 3 for [[5,1,3]]; Knill-Laflamme deviation 0 for |E| <= 2.
cycles.falsification_criterion: Any non-integer I(R:A) for a stabilizer code, or KL violation for |E| <= 2.
cycles.method: experiments/h_qec_islands.py: n = 5,7,9,11, 40/40/30/16 seeds, SeedSequence([20261115, family, n, seed]); exact enumeration of erasure subsets.
cycles.result: [[5,1,3]] exactly perfect; random-code distance distribution e.g. n=11: d=3 in 10/16; Haar I(R:A)+I(R:E) = 2 ln 2 to 1e-10; Page-type approximation gap 0.028 -> 0.0006 bits for n = 5 -> 11.
cycles.verification: verify/independent_upgrade.py V2 (seed 20261116, numpy, no eh/ import): agree=True; [[5,1,3]] built from its stabilizer generators, all 30 erasure patterns |A| = 1..4 checked.
critic_objections: 'New closed form' F_Petz = Tr_E[(Tr_R sqrt(rho_RE))^2]/d_R is the complementary-channel form of the standard Petz fidelity (same as Track C's pure-state formula); novelty claim retracted, now 're-derived'.
Random-code distance statistics are specific to the 10n-gate circuit ensemble.
Haar 'distance' is undefined (no exact correction); kept only with the distance_note.
cycles.status: confirmed; novelty claim on Petz closed form retracted
cycles.conclusion: [[5,1,3]] exactly perfect; random-code distance distribution e.g. n=11: d=3 in 10/16; Haar I(R:A)+I(R:E) = 2 ln 2 to 1e-10; Page-type approximation gap 0.028 -> 0.0006 bits for n = 5 -> 11.

cycles.question: Does a semiclassical island formula (AMM eternal-BH model) reproduce a Page-like curve, and how does its shape compare with the qubit Page curve?
cycles.hypothesis: Extremizing the generalized entropy gives a QES at a* matching the AMM asymptotic, and S(R) saturates at t_Page.
assumptions: Semiclassical gravity formula (JT + CFT, c = 24, beta = 2 pi), not a circuit simulation
The shape comparison with qubit Page curves is illustrative only: different models, no shared parameters
cycles.prediction: a* within 1% of AMM asymptotic; late no-island slope = 2 pi c/(3 beta).
cycles.falsification_criterion: Multiple or no extrema, or slope mismatch.
cycles.method: experiments/h_qec_islands.py islands: numerical extremization on a grid, phi_r scan.
cycles.result: a* = 4.0386 vs AMM asymptotic 3.9957 (rel. err 0.0049 -> 0.0009 as phi_r grows); slope 8.0 = 2 pi c/(3 beta); t_Page = 66.29 equals the leading-order formula.
cycles.verification: Internal: slope and t_Page match closed forms in results/h_qec_islands.json; not re-derived by a separate code path in this pass.
critic_objections: This evaluates a published formula; it does not test or derive the island formula, and the qubit circuits say nothing about it.
Agreement with AMM is agreement of a numerical extremum with its own asymptotic expansion: class 1.
cycles.conclusion: a* = 4.0386 vs AMM asymptotic 3.9957 (rel. err 0.0049 -> 0.0009 as phi_r grows); slope 8.0 = 2 pi c/(3 beta); t_Page = 66.29 equals the leading-order formula.

figures.title: Page curve of Haar-random states, N = 8..24
figures.caption: Numerics (dots, +-1 std band over states) against Page's exact formula; deficit near the Page time with 95% CI; z-scores of all 213 (N, k) cells (max |z| = 3.38 at N = 24 with 8 states). Haar-random pure qubit states, no gravity.

figures.title: Page's theorem at 124 (m, n) pairs
figures.caption: Finite-size deficit at m = n, error of the asymptotic forms (exact arithmetic), z-scores (max 2.69, rms 1.00) and Monte Carlo convergence (slope -0.476, expected -0.5).

figures.title: Sequential Haar evaporation
figures.caption: Mean S(R) per step (+-1 std over seeds), deviation from Page, distribution tests (N = 10: smallest p = 0.055 over 53 tests), runtime and memory on the A100. Literal protocol to N = 14, isometry sampler to N = 26.

figures.title: Bell-pair model versus unitary evaporation
figures.caption: S(R) = k ln 2 for independent pairs against the unitary model and the assumed capacity (N - k) ln 2; the two part at k = N/2. The capacity is an assumption of the toy.

figures.title: Radiation entropy by scrambler
figures.caption: Sequential evaporation with open-chain brickwork scramblers of different families and depths; bands are 95% CI over seeds.

figures.title: Deviation from Page and scrambling depth
figures.caption: Max over steps of (Page - <S>) versus depth per emission (local Haar, Clifford) and one-shot half-cut scrambling depth (Haar: D* = 1.87 N + 1.9, eps = 0.05 nats). Error bars 95% CI. Negative Clifford cells are single noisy cells; the stabilizer ensemble mean is below Page.

figures.title: Deviation from Page versus system size
figures.caption: Deviation versus N for fixed depth, and cost scaling on one A100. Seed counts shrink with N (4 at N = 26).

figures.title: Entanglement spectrum at the half cut
figures.caption: S_vN - S_2 per step and the mean sorted spectrum; stabilizer states have exactly flat spectra. Error bars 95% CI.

figures.title: Hayden-Preskill mutual information
figures.caption: I(R:Bob) versus emitted qubits m; old-hole curves collapse for all n_B, young-hole curves shift by about n_B/2. Bands are std over seeds (4-200).

figures.title: Decoupling of the reference from the remaining hole
figures.caption: Measured trace distance T against the finite-d bound and 1/2 * 2^(k-m); measured/bound = 0.83-0.87 at k = 1, n_B = 4. Error bars 95% CI.

figures.title: Decoder fidelities
figures.caption: Uhlmann fidelity (lower bound on the optimal decoder) and Yoshida-Kitaev probabilistic decoder fidelity F_EPR versus m.

figures.title: Recovery thresholds versus hole size
figures.caption: Integer thresholds read from seed-mean curves (no error bars): old hole essentially independent of n_B, young hole about n_B/2 + k + const.

figures.title: Hayden-Preskill with local scramblers
figures.caption: Open-chain brickwork on 10 qubits, 32 seeds, near/far diary placement; far placement needs depth about 24-32 to reach the Haar thresholds. One size only.

figures.title: Renyi Page curves, N = 12
figures.caption: Haar random pure states (random-matrix model, no gravity), 400 seeds; S_n for n = 1/2,1,2,3,inf vs exact S_1 (Page) and -log Lubkin purity.

figures.title: Entanglement spectrum vs Marchenko-Pastur
figures.caption: Haar Schmidt spectra against the MP law with O(1/d) finite-size corrections; asymptotic random-matrix law, finite d.

figures.title: Haar vs stabilizer vs brickwork spectra
figures.caption: Renyi and flatness diagnostics separating Haar, random-stabilizer (6N Clifford brickwork) and shallow Haar brickwork states.

figures.title: Petz recovery: old vs young hole
figures.caption: Haar scrambler, k = 1, n_B = 3..7, 24 seeds; Petz decoder (sigma = 1/d_M) is one decoder, so thresholds are decoder-specific.

figures.title: Recovery under noise and finite depth
figures.caption: Depolarizing noise on emitted qubits and brickwork depth; Haar and Clifford scramblers, small N.

figures.title: Infinite-temperature OTOC vs depth
figures.caption: F(t) = 2^-N Tr[W(t) V W(t)^dag V^dag], Pauli W, V; Haar/2-design value -1/(d^2-1). OTOC decay is necessary, not sufficient, for recovery.

figures.title: Erasure correction: [[5,1,3]], stabilizer, Haar codes
figures.caption: Finite-dimensional QEC models; I(R:A) and Petz fidelity vs erased qubits. Does not derive holography.

figures.title: Island-formula Page curve (AMM model)
figures.caption: Semiclassical JT+CFT formula evaluated numerically (c = 24, beta = 2 pi); kept separate from the qubit models, which do not test it.

tests.command: /opt/anaconda3/bin/python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/ (run as 4 parallel file groups)

verification.disagreement: Builder hand-off report said scrambled Clifford states sit above Page by about 0.19 nats at the half cut; the mean is below Page by 0.088 +- 0.015 nats (N = 10, 800 states). Corrected in README.md, notes/critic.md and the paper; no repository file contained the wrong sentence.
verification.not_reverified: Large-N GPU numbers were checked for internal consistency of the stored JSON only, not re-run; one small CPU point each of C, E1 and E2 was reproduced.

artifact.hero_caption: A Schwarzschild black hole ray-traced on an A100: 24 million light rays integrated along exact null geodesics around a thin Keplerian accretion disk (ISCO to 13 r_s) with a Novikov-Thorne temperature profile, gravitational redshift and Doppler beaming. The far side of the disk is lensed over and under the shadow; the thin ring is the photon ring. A simulation, not a photograph; the gas texture is procedural. Source: viz/blackhole/raytrace.py.
